stories.headline: Meta Llama Approaches Frontier Capability as Open-Source Models Close the Gap
stories.excerpt: Meta's latest Llama release narrowed the performance gap with proprietary frontier models to single-digit percentages across major benchmarks. Enterprise adoption is accelerating as companies reconsider vendor lock-in, with AI-related GitHub repositories growing 178 percent year-over-year to exceed 4.3 million projects.
stories.licenceBasis: TechCrunch RSS excerpt with link-out, per feed terms of use

stories.headline: BepiColombo Enters Mercury Orbit After Seven-Year Journey, Begins Surface Mapping
stories.excerpt: The joint ESA-JAXA BepiColombo mission successfully entered orbit around Mercury after a seven-year interplanetary cruise. The spacecraft's two orbiters will spend at least one year mapping Mercury's surface, magnetic field, and exosphere, providing the most detailed study of the solar system's innermost planet to date.

stories.headline: Warsh's Five Fed Task Forces Signal Structural Overhaul of Monetary Policy Operations
stories.excerpt: New Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's creation of five internal Task Forces — covering communications, the balance sheet, data sources, productivity and jobs, and the inflation framework — signals the most significant restructuring of Fed operations in decades. Each task force will report recommendations before year-end.
stories.licenceBasis: Federal Reserve public domain — official minutes and statements

stories.headline: Adobe Breached Via Indian BPO Firm: Threat Actor 'Mr. Raccoon' Used Phishing to Reach Helpdesk
stories.excerpt: A threat actor known as 'Mr. Raccoon' allegedly breached Adobe through an Indian Business Process Outsourcing firm, delivering a Remote Access Tool via targeted phishing emails to reach the helpdesk environment. The incident highlights growing supply-chain attack vectors through third-party service providers.

stories.headline: Global Electric Vehicle Sales Top 20 Million Units as Battery Costs Hit Record Lows
stories.excerpt: Global EV sales surpassed 20 million units in the first eight months of 2026, driven by plunging battery costs and expanded model availability across all price segments. China accounts for over half of global sales, while European and North American markets show strong double-digit growth.
stories.licenceBasis: AI synthesis from Earth.Org and IEA data

stories.headline: EDIT-101 CRISPR Therapy Approved for Leber Congenital Amaurosis, Restoring Vision in Genetic Blindness
stories.excerpt: The FDA approved EDIT-101, a CRISPR-based in-vivo gene editing therapy for Leber congenital amaurosis type 10, a rare genetic form of childhood blindness. The treatment directly edits photoreceptor cells in the retina, making it only the second CRISPR therapy to receive full regulatory approval.

stories.headline: Anthropic Ships Claude Agent SDK With TypeScript and Python Tools for Production Agent Systems
stories.excerpt: Anthropic released the Claude Agent SDK, providing specialized TypeScript and Python tooling designed to integrate Claude models into production agent systems. The SDK includes built-in support for tool use orchestration, multi-step reasoning, and structured output, lowering the barrier for developers building autonomous AI workflows.
stories.licenceBasis: Hacker News public API — titles and links, discussion linked out

stories.headline: EU AI Act Enforcement Phase Begins With Compliance Deadlines for High-Risk Systems
stories.excerpt: The European Union's AI Act entered its enforcement phase, with companies operating high-risk AI systems now required to demonstrate compliance with transparency, safety, and human oversight requirements. Non-compliant organizations face fines of up to 7% of global annual revenue.
stories.licenceBasis: AI synthesis from Reuters and EU Commission announcements

stories.headline: 2026 Breakthrough Prize Awards $3 Million for Pioneering Gene Replacement Therapy
stories.excerpt: The Breakthrough Prize Foundation awarded the 2026 Life Sciences prize to Jean Bennett, Katherine High, and Albert Maguire for developing the first FDA-approved gene replacement therapy, which treats Leber congenital amaurosis by replacing the defective RPE65 gene. The $3 million prize recognizes work that opened the door to an entire class of genetic medicines.

stories.headline: 721 Ransomware Victims Recorded in June Alone as Attack Pace Remains Elevated
stories.excerpt: Cybersecurity monitoring firms recorded 721 publicly disclosed ransomware victims globally in June 2026, continuing the elevated attack pace that has defined the year. The United States remained the single most-targeted country, with healthcare, education, and critical infrastructure sectors bearing the heaviest impact.
stories.licenceBasis: AI synthesis from NVD and cybersecurity industry reports

stories.headline: Japan's MMX Mission Launches for Martian Moon Phobos to Collect First-Ever Samples
stories.excerpt: The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency launched its Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, sending a spacecraft on a multi-year journey to the Martian moon Phobos. The mission aims to land on Phobos, collect surface samples, and return them to Earth — a feat never before attempted at Mars.

stories.headline: Ireland Closes Its Last Coal Plant, Joining Growing List of Coal-Free Nations
stories.excerpt: Ireland officially closed its last remaining coal-fired power station, becoming one of a growing number of nations to fully exit coal-based electricity generation. The closure is part of Ireland's broader commitment to reach 80% renewable electricity by 2030.
stories.licenceBasis: NOAA public domain climate and energy data

stories.headline: Open-Source Foundation Models Breaking the Grip of AI Giants in Post-Training Innovation
stories.excerpt: Breakthroughs in the post-training phase of open-source AI models are enabling unprecedented customization and fine-tuning for specific applications, challenging the dominance of proprietary frontier models. Researchers report that open models now achieve comparable results on domain-specific tasks at a fraction of the inference cost.
stories.licenceBasis: AI synthesis from InfoWorld and industry analysis

stories.headline: ASEAN Summit Agrees on Cross-Border Digital Payment Interoperability by 2028
stories.excerpt: Leaders at the ASEAN Economic Summit agreed to a binding timeline for cross-border digital payment interoperability across all ten member states by 2028. The agreement builds on existing bilateral QR payment links between Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia, extending the framework to cover the full bloc.
stories.licenceBasis: AI synthesis from Reuters and ASEAN Secretariat statements

stories.headline: CRISPR-Based Treatment for Hereditary Angioedema Shows Strong Results in Phase III Trial
stories.excerpt: A Phase III clinical trial of a CRISPR-based therapy for hereditary angioedema reported a 95% reduction in attack frequency compared to placebo, potentially offering a one-time cure for the painful and sometimes life-threatening swelling disorder that affects roughly 1 in 50,000 people worldwide.
